name: semantic-crosscheck
description: Cross-layer verification for an ontology plus semantic layer on PostgreSQL 17, for Codex and Claude Code.

interface.shortDescription: Prove that a PostgreSQL closure, SHACL rules, OWL reasoning and a Cube model agree.
interface.longDescription: Release v0.16.0: cross-check PostgreSQL 17 closures, SQL/SHACL rules, OWL/HermiT and Cube against independently authored gold SQL. V4 replays every eligible bounded V3 pair chunk and its NULL group, retaining per-mutant execution coverage with safe item ids, attempts and unexecuted reasons. A separate positive mutant_max_items budget defaults to 10000; exhaustion is not_run, never survival. Optional OWL inconsistency explanations can enumerate verified alternative subset-minimal generated-group cores, with a default result cap of 1, default node cap of 256 and hard ceilings of 32 results and 4096 nodes. Enumeration shares existing check/time budgets and preserves the original consistency failure and first-core fields. Coverage receipts and explanation completeness add no report authority or business certification. Existing report requirements and dependency pins remain unchanged. Rerun operational stages after upgrading.
defaultPrompt: Use semantic-crosscheck to run the synthetic demo end to end.
Use semantic-crosscheck to verify my crosscheck.toml against PostgreSQL and explain what is not proven.
